read.passage: Every day, millions of images and stories go viral before anyone has checked whether they are true. Fact-checkers argue that the problem is not a lack of information but a lack of patience. Rarely do people stop to ask who created a post, or why. Yet a few simple habits can make a real difference. First, look for the original source: a claim that cannot be traced back to a named person or organisation should be treated with caution. Second, cross-check the story with at least two reliable news outlets. Third, notice your own emotions. Posts designed to make us angry or afraid are, by and large, the ones most likely to be misleading. None of this requires special training; it simply requires us to pause before we press 'share'.
